stories.title: GTA VI's launch-day credits reveal its long-hidden cast
paragraphs: After years of secrecy, launch-day credits and reporting began identifying the actors and voices behind characters in Grand Theft Auto VI, including its central Vice City cast.
The new cast details are a distinct development from the release and livestream audience figures Owl covered earlier. A sampled r/GTA6 post naming Dylan Rourke and Manni L.

scoreNotes.general: A new, highly visible piece of launch-day information for one of the year's most anticipated games, supported by AP reporting and a strong sampled fan response.
scoreNotes.heat: The cast reveal adds a shareable discovery to a major global release, and the sampled subreddit post drew thousands of votes.
scoreNotes.time: AP's report appeared during this edition's 24-hour window, after Owl's previous coverage.
scoreNotes.ethos: AP reports the cast and voice revelations; the Reddit vote count is a point-in-time signal from one community, not a measure of broad opinion.

stories.title: Euro Truck Simulator 2 sets a 14-year Steam player record after new DLC
paragraphs: Euro Truck Simulator 2 reached 101,783 concurrent players on Steam on November 15, its highest peak in 14 years. GamesRadar linked the surge to the game's recent DLC releases.
The result shows how a steady expansion pipeline can bring a long-running simulation back to record audience levels. It is a Steam player count, not a sales figure or a count across consoles.

scoreNotes.general: A rare audience spike for a long-running simulation game is a useful signal about the reach of established franchises and expansion releases.
scoreNotes.heat: The game crossed 100,000 concurrent Steam players and reached a new all-time peak after a 14-year run.
scoreNotes.time: The record occurred November 15, so it falls in the seven-day window but outside the fresh 24-hour window.
scoreNotes.ethos: GamesRadar and SteamDB both report the 101,783-player peak; the figure measures Steam concurrency, not total sales or players across platforms.

stories.title: YouTube promotes a new slate of creator-led entertainment
paragraphs: YouTube introduced its next Creator Premieres slate, describing a new wave of creator-led entertainment and daily short-form point-of-view episodes.

The company also highlighted a special premiering November 25 on the Happy Hour with Ina channel. The move gives selected creator programming a scheduled, platform-promoted launch rather than relying only on each channel's regular uploads.

scoreNotes.general: The announcement points to YouTube's continued investment in packaging creator-led shows as scheduled entertainment, though the saved evidence gives limited detail on the full slate.
scoreNotes.heat: The slate spans creator-led programming and scheduled premieres on a platform with a large entertainment audience.
scoreNotes.time: Broadcast reported the announcement on November 18, within seven days but outside the current 24-hour window.
scoreNotes.ethos: YouTube's blog and Broadcast confirm the slate; only a few program details are visible in the saved search results.
